transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’ve felt low and weighed down almost all the time for the last couple of years, and it just never really lifts. My primary care doctor suggested I come speak with someone because of how long it's been going on.
During these two years, have you experienced any periods where you lost interest in activities that you normally enjoy, or have you been able to find pleasure in things most of the time?

Yes, I've definitely lost interest in the things I used to love. Over the last two years, my favorite hobbies—like precision baking, stargazing with my telescope, and planning trips—have started to feel like stressful obligations rather than pleasures. I honestly can't remember the last time I felt genuinely happy or relaxed while doing any of them.

Can you tell me if these feelings of being low and losing interest in activities have been constant over the two years, or have you had periods where your mood and interest in activities improved for a while before worsening again?

They have been pretty much constant ever since we moved here a little over two years ago. I haven't had any real periods of improvement or relief, just short stretches of a few days at most where the feeling is slightly less heavy before it returns. It has just been a continuous, ongoing weight.

Have you experienced any significant changes or variations in the intensity of your low mood or loss of interest over the two years, such as periods with more pronounced symptoms or brief moments of near-normal functioning?

No, there haven't really been any breaks or times where I felt close to normal. It has been almost entirely continuous since our move, and I honestly can't recall the last time I felt genuinely light or happy for more than a few minutes at a time. It's just been a constant, unchanging weight.
Have you noticed any seasonal patterns to your low mood, or does it seem to remain constant regardless of the time of year or other external factors?

No, there aren't any seasonal patterns to how I feel. This low, heavy feeling has been completely constant and continuous ever since we moved over two years ago, regardless of the time of year or the weather. It just stays the same day in and day out.

Can you describe any periods, no matter how brief, where you felt your normal self again or had a significant reduction in these feelings of being low and disconnected from activities, even if it was just for a day or two?

No, I haven't had any periods where I felt like my normal self or experienced a real lift in my mood. At most, I might feel slightly lighter for just a few minutes at a time, but never for a whole day or even a few hours. It has just been a continuous weight ever since we moved over two years ago.

Have you had any episodes of significantly elevated mood, increased energy, or decreased need for sleep that lasted for a few days to a week or more at any point in your life, or has your mood been consistently low as you've described?

No, I have never experienced anything like that. I've never had periods of high energy, elevated mood, or needing less sleep. My mood has just been consistently low, flat, and weighed down for the past two years without any of those high periods.
Have you ever experienced any unusual thoughts, heard voices, or seen things that others couldn't, during these two years or at any other time in your life?

No, I have never experienced anything like that or seen or heard things that aren't there. My struggles are strictly related to this heavy low mood, constant fatigue, and the mental fog I've been dealing with.

Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'constant' and 'continuous' when describing your low mood over the past two years, and have you experienced any subtle variations in your symptoms that might not be immediately noticeable to you?

When I say constant, I mean that I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling in my chest almost every single day without fail since we moved. It doesn't lift for any meaningful stretch of time, and at most, I might get a brief distraction for a few minutes. I truly cannot remember a single period where I felt genuinely happy or light for any real length of time.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over the past two years, or have they remained relatively stable?
No, I haven't really noticed any significant changes in that area. My appetite and weight have remained relatively stable over the past two years.
Have you experienced any changes in your sleep patterns over the past two years, such as insomnia or sleeping more than usual?

I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my sleep patterns, and I still get about eight hours of sleep. However, I wake up feeling completely exhausted, like I'm wading through molasses all day anyway.
Have you been experiencing excessive guilt or feelings of worthlessness over the past two years, or is that not something you've struggled with?

No, I haven't really struggled with feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt. Those specific feelings don't really stand out to me compared to the constant exhaustion and flatness I feel every day.

You've mentioned losing interest in activities you used to enjoy, but can you tell me if there are any activities, no matter how small they might seem, that you still find some pleasure or satisfaction in, even if it's not as fulfilling as it used to be?

Honestly, there aren't really any activities that bring me pleasure or satisfaction right now. Even my former favorite hobbies—like precision baking, stargazing, or planning trips—just feel like flat obligations or chores rather than things I actually enjoy.
Are there any small, everyday tasks or routines that you still find slightly enjoyable or that give you a tiny sense of accomplishment, even if it's not related to your former hobbies?

Honestly, nothing really brings me a sense of accomplishment or enjoyment right now. Even basic daily tasks like unloading the dishwasher or deciding what to wear feel incredibly exhausting and heavy. Everything just feels flat and pointless.

Can you confirm if your symptoms have been present for more than two years without any significant improvement, and if so, have you experienced any periods of at least two months where your symptoms were not present?

Yes, this low feeling has been present continuously for a little over two years now, starting shortly after our move. I definitely have not had any periods of two months where the symptoms went away; at most, I've had very short stretches of slight relief, but never a real break from the heaviness.

You've described a continuous low mood for over two years without significant improvement. Can you think of any factors, such as life events or changes, that might have triggered this persistent low mood, or did it seem to start without any clear cause?

Yes, it started shortly after my spouse and I relocated from Southern California to the Bay Area for my promotion to senior physical scientist a little over two years ago. The move completely disrupted my daily routines and social support, and the stress of my demanding new role combined with my spouse struggling to find comparable work has created a lot of tension at home.

Can you clarify if there have been any periods, even brief, where your symptoms seemed to partially improve or significantly worsen in relation to specific events or changes in your life, such as work stress or relationship issues, since your move?

The symptoms have been pretty much continuous since the move, with no real improvement other than brief moments lasting a few minutes that never actually lift. Instead, the heavy feeling has steadily worsened alongside growing tension at home, culminating in a recent tense argument where my spouse called me "unreachable" for over a year. That argument is what finally prompted me to seek help, as I realized how much this is hurting our relationship.

You've mentioned that your symptoms started after your move and have been continuous since then, but can you clarify if there were any periods, no matter how brief, where you felt your symptoms were significantly worse or better in relation to specific events, such as the recent argument with your spouse, which might indicate a pattern or variation in your symptoms?

No, the argument didn't actually make my depression feel any deeper, as my mood has stayed remarkably constant and flat rather than fluctuating with specific events. It was more of a wake-up call because my spouse pointed out how emotionally absent and "unreachable" I've been for over a year. I really haven't experienced any periods of feeling significantly better or worse; it has just been a continuous, heavy state for the last two years.

Can you think of any periods, even if very brief, where you felt a significant reduction in your low mood and loss of interest in activities, which might have lasted for at least a couple of weeks, or has it been a completely unbroken stretch of feeling low?

It has been a completely unbroken stretch of feeling low ever since we moved over two years ago. I have definitely not had any periods of relief or feeling better that lasted for two weeks; at most, any slight lift in my mood only lasts for a few minutes before the heaviness returns.

Given that your symptoms have been continuous for over two years without significant improvement, can you confirm if you've ever had a period of at least two months within these two years where you didn't experience any significant depressive symptoms, or have the symptoms been persistently present the entire time?

I can confirm that the symptoms have been persistently present the entire time. There has never been a period of two months—or even close to that—where I felt back to normal. Any brief moments of relief have only lasted for very short stretches of a few minutes at most.

You've consistently described your symptoms as continuous and unbroken over the past two years, but can you think of any instance, no matter how small, where you felt like you were starting to come out of this low mood, even if it didn't last, which might help differentiate between a persistent depressive disorder and a major depressive disorder?

No, I really can't think of any instance where I felt like I was starting to come out of this low mood. While I might have had a few fleeting minutes where I wasn't completely overwhelmed, the heavy, gray feeling has never truly lifted for more than a couple of days at most. It has just kept me constantly weighed down without any real gap.
To clarify, you've had no periods of two months or more without significant depressive symptoms over the past two years, correct?

Yes, that is correct. I have definitely not had any periods of two months, or even two weeks, where this heavy feeling went away. It has been completely continuous and unbroken the entire time since we moved.

Can you confirm if there has ever been a time during these two years where you felt your low mood significantly lift for at least a short period, such as a few days, which might indicate a difference between a persistent depressive disorder and other types of depression?

No, it has never lifted for a period like a few days. At most, I might feel slightly lighter for just a few minutes at a time, but the heavy feeling quickly returns. It has been almost completely constant over the last two years.

Can you think of any situation, event, or circumstance under which your low mood or loss of interest might slightly improve, even if temporarily, or are they completely unaffected by any external factors or changes in your life?

My low mood feels almost completely unaffected by external changes. Even when I try to spend time with my spouse or do things I used to love, like baking or stargazing, any lighter feeling only lasts for a few minutes at most before the heavy, gray feeling returns. It has been this way continuously for over two years now.

Is it possible that if you were to experience a significant change in your life circumstances, such as a resolution to the tension at home or a change in your work environment, you might see some improvement in your mood, or do you feel that your low mood would persist regardless of such changes?

Honestly, I can't picture things feeling any different even if those circumstances changed. I feel completely stuck in this flat, numb place, and it feels like no amount of external change or effort is going to make a difference. I just can't imagine this heavy feeling ever lifting.

Given your consistent description of a continuous, unbroken low mood for over two years, can you confirm one last time if there has ever been any period, no matter how brief, where you felt like you were returning to your normal self or experiencing a significant reduction in your depressive symptoms?

Yes, I can confirm that. There have been absolutely no periods where I felt like my normal self or experienced any real relief over the last two years. Any moments where the heaviness lifted even slightly lasted only for a few minutes at a time before the gray feeling returned.

Considering your symptoms have been constant for over two years without any significant breaks, do you think it's possible that you might have experienced a major depressive episode at some point in the past, even if it was before this continuous period began?
No, I don't recall ever having any episodes like this before our move two years ago. This is the very first time in my life that I have experienced such a prolonged and heavy period of depression.

Before this two-year period, did you ever experience any episodes of depression that lasted for at least two weeks, which might help differentiate between a persistent depressive disorder and other types of depression?

No, I don't recall experiencing any similar episodes of depression before our move two years ago. My mood was generally stable back then, and this is the first time I've ever felt this kind of prolonged heaviness.
